expectations.text: All docstrings use triple double quotes ("""), none use ''' or single-line ' quotes
expectations.evidence: Every docstring opens/closes with """ (lines 1, 18, 34, 51, 72, 86, 116); no ''' or single-quote docstrings anywhere.

expectations.text: Module, class, and every public method have a docstring; multi-line docstrings have a one-sentence first line ending with a period, then a blank line
expectations.evidence: All seven docstrings present; each starts with one sentence ending in a period followed by a blank line, e.g. line 1 "In-memory retry queue with exponential backoff scheduling." then blank line 2; line 86 "Records a failed attempt and reschedules or evicts the task." then blank line 87.

expectations.text: First lines are descriptive ("Schedules...", "Returns..."), not imperative ("Schedule...", "Return...")
next_ready_at documents the -1.0 sentinel meaning (task unknown/not pending)
expectations.evidence: Line 78: "The task's ready timestamp, or -1.0 if the task is not pending."

expectations.text: mark_failed documents KeyError for unknown task_id (Raises:) and the None return meaning the task was dropped after exhausting attempts
expectations.evidence: Lines 101-102: "Raises:\n    KeyError: If ``task_id`` is not currently pending." Lines 98-99: "or None if the task exhausted its attempts and was dropped."

expectations.text: drain_ready is documented with a Yields: section (not Returns:) and mentions that drained tasks are removed from the queue
expectations.evidence: Lines 125-126: "Yields:\n    Tuples of ``(task_id, payload)`` for each ready task." plus lines 118-119: "Tasks are removed from the queue as they are yielded". No Returns: section.

expectations.text: schedule's Returns: explains the True/False semantics (False = task_id already pending, call ignored)
expectations.evidence: Lines 62-63: "True if the task was newly scheduled, False if a task with the same ID was already pending." plus Args note line 54-55: "Scheduling an ID that is already pending is a no-op."

expectations.text: Args: sections list each parameter with expected types (code has no annotations) and consistent continuation indentation
expectations.evidence: Continuation indentation is consistent (4-space hang), but no Args entry states a type: line 37 "max_attempts: Maximum attempts allowed per task. Must be >= 1.", line 54 "task_id: Unique identifier for the task.", line 56 "payload: Arbitrary data associated with the task" — no int/float/str given for any parameter despite the unannotated code.

expectations.text: No comments that merely restate the code (e.g. '# increment attempts' style)
expectations.evidence: Three comments, all informative: line 47 "# Maps task_id -> [payload, attempt_count, ready_at_timestamp].", lines 110-111 "# Exponential backoff: base_delay after the first failure, doubling with each subsequent failure.", line 129 "# Snapshot the keys since entries are deleted during iteration." — none merely restate code.

summary.notes: Accurate and complete documentation (in Sphinx-flavored style) that fails only the requirement to state explicit parameter types in Args sections.
